verdict.summary: Marsh is a resilient insurance-brokerage and consulting compounder, but Q2 was solid rather than uniformly strong. Revenue rose 6% to $7.4 billion and 5% on an underlying basis; GAAP EPS increased 7% to $2.63 and adjusted EPS rose 9% to $2.96. Consulting led with 8% underlying growth, including 13% at Marsh Management Consulting, while Risk and Insurance Services grew only 3% underlying and Guy Carpenter declined 2%. The business benefits from recurring client relationships, premium growth, specialized data and advisory talent, but it carries $22.38 billion of reported debt and remains exposed to insurance pricing, claims-related liability and acquisition integration. Capital returns are tangible: Marsh repurchased $750 million in Q2 and increased the quarterly dividend 10% to $0.99. The B- grade is unchanged. The preserved $192.98/$187.93/$195.67/$198.49 plan is rejected at only 0.53R/1.09R.

business.overview:
Marsh earns fees and commissions by placing insurance and reinsurance, advising clients on risk and capital, and selling consulting services through Mercer and Marsh Management Consulting. Q2 revenue split roughly $4.8 billion for Risk and Insurance Services and $2.6 billion for Consulting.

The AI transmission channel is productivity and advisory content. Better modeling can improve risk selection, placement analytics, workforce advice and consulting delivery; the Oliver Wyman-Anthropic relationship may deepen those tools. Revenue still depends on client retention, insurance pricing, exposure growth and billable expertise, not software-seat growth.

The model breaks if insurance rates soften faster than exposure grows, litigation or fiduciary claims rise, cyber incidents damage trust, or acquisitions fail to earn their cost of capital. Talent inflation can also absorb revenue growth because compensation is the largest operating expense. Guy Carpenter's Q2 decline shows that scale does not eliminate cyclical pockets.
business.moat: Marsh's moat is a global network across insurance placement, reinsurance, actuarial data, benefits and management consulting. Client relationships, proprietary loss and pricing data, carrier access and specialist talent reinforce one another. The moat is durable but people-dependent: key-team departures, conflicts, regulation and technology-driven disintermediation can erode it.

earnings.beatNote: Q2 2026 GAAP revenue rose 6% to $7.4B and operating income rose 4% to $1.9B. GAAP diluted EPS was $2.63, up 7%; non-GAAP adjusted EPS rose 9% to $2.96 and adjusted operating income rose 5% to $2.2B. Risk and Insurance Services grew 3% underlying, Consulting grew 8%, Marsh Risk grew 4%, and Guy Carpenter declined 2%. No formal full-year revenue or EPS range was issued in the release. The key caveat is mix: first-half GAAP operating income fell 5%, and reinsurance broking lagged stronger consulting growth. The official corporate calendar and filings reviewed through August 28 do not announce the next earnings date, so it remains not confirmed.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: Marsh repurchased approximately 4.5M shares for $750M in Q2 and 8.7M shares for $1.5B in the first half, while the board raised the quarterly dividend 10% to $0.99. The reviewed 10-Q and 10-K show normal equity-compensation and repurchase activity, with no reviewed prospectus supplement establishing an ATM. The central capital risk is leverage rather than dilution: reported debt is $22.38B, cash is $1.70B, and acquisition spending must earn above financing costs while buybacks continue. Marsh does not provide a current fully diluted point-in-time bridge in the reviewed materials, so awards are not added to the basic count heuristically.

filings.finding: The June 2026 Form 10-Q reports $7.404 billion Q2 revenue, $1.899 billion operating income, $2.63 GAAP diluted EPS and segment detail showing stronger Consulting than reinsurance growth.

The 2025 Form 10-K establishes Marsh's global brokerage and consulting mix, debt and acquisition obligations, professional-liability exposure, compensation intensity and controls underlying the 2026 quality assessment.
The July 21 Form 8-K furnished the direct earnings exhibit showing 5% Q2 underlying revenue growth, $2.96 adjusted EPS, $750 million of repurchases and no formal full-year EPS range.
